faqs.question: How can I record a football match with my phone?
faqs.answer: Place the phone near the halfway line, raise it above head height, use landscape orientation and keep as much of the pitch visible as possible. Mount it securely, check battery and storage, then record the full match without moving the phone.

No. One phone can work when it captures the full small-sided pitch clearly. Pitchside recommends two phones where possible, with one facing each goal, because this can provide clearer coverage of both halves.
faqs.question: Do I need two phones to use Pitchside?
Where should I position the phones?
faqs.answer: Position the phones near the halfway line and above head height. For a two-phone setup, point one phone toward each goal. Keep fencing, spectators and substitutes from blocking the view.

faqs.question: Can Pitchside create highlights from my recording?
faqs.answer: Pitchside is being developed to process full match recordings and generate key football highlights. It is currently in private beta, so output quality continues to improve as more small-sided footage is processed.

faqs.question: What football statistics can Pitchside produce?
faqs.answer: The planned first-release statistics include goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles assigned to teams and individual players, together with player leaderboards. Detection and player assignment are still improving during beta.

faqs.question: Which football formats does Pitchside support?
faqs.answer: Pitchside currently focuses on 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side football. The model is being trained specifically around the camera angles, pace and crowded spaces found in real small-sided matches.

faqs.question: Do I need a specialist football camera?
faqs.answer: No. Pitchside is designed around footage recorded with ordinary phones. A secure mount, useful camera height and a clear view of the pitch matter more than buying a dedicated football camera.

faqs.question: How long does Pitchside take to process a match?
faqs.answer: During the current private beta, uploading and processing can take up to 45 minutes. The exact time can vary with the recording length, connection and developing upload workflow.

faqs.question: Will a ball-tracking tripod work with Pitchside?
faqs.answer: A ball-tracking tripod may work if it keeps the main action visible and produces stable footage. A fixed elevated view can also work well because it gives the model a consistent view of the playing area.

contentBlocks.content: Record a Football Match Without an Expensive Camera

Professional football recording systems can be useful, but their specialist cameras, subscriptions and fixed setups are often more than an amateur team needs. Pitchside takes a simpler route: use one or two phones to record the match, then use the footage to create something more useful than a long video sitting in your camera roll.

For a Sunday League team, small-sided group or regular kickabout, the best recording system is usually the one that is easy enough to use every week. A stable phone, a clear view of the pitch and a consistent setup make Pitchside a practical football camera app without asking your club to buy dedicated recording hardware.

items: No specialist football camera is required.
No camera operator needs to follow the ball for the full match.
One-phone and two-phone recording setups are supported.
The same repeatable setup can be used for future fixtures.
The goal is to turn ordinary phone footage into highlights and match data.

contentBlocks.content: How Recording With Pitchside Works

Recording a football match with Pitchside is designed to fit around the way grassroots teams already play. Set up the phone or phones before kick-off, record the game from a stable position, then upload the footage for processing when the match finishes.
1. Position the phone
Place the phone close to the halfway line and raise it above head height. Keep the pitch unobstructed and avoid a position where substitutes, spectators or fencing repeatedly block the view.
2. Record the full match

Start recording before kick-off and let the phone capture the game from a fixed, landscape view. Check storage, battery level and lens cleanliness before the match so the recording is not interrupted.
3. Upload the footage
After full-time, upload the recording to Pitchside. If you used two phones, the footage from both sides can be brought together to provide broader coverage of the match.
4. Receive the match output

Pitchside processes the video to identify match events and create useful output. The first release is being developed around highlights and core team and player statistics rather than leaving you to review the entire recording manually.
Record With One Phone or Two Phones

You can record a football match with one phone, but two phones are the preferred Pitchside setup. The right choice depends on the pitch size, the height available for the phones and how much of the playing area one camera can capture clearly.

cells: One phone
Near the halfway line, above head height, with the full pitch visible where possible
Smaller pitches, simple weekly recording and teams testing the workflow
Play at the far edges may be smaller or harder to see
Two phones
Both near halfway, with one phone facing each goal
Clearer coverage of both halves and better visibility around each goal
Requires two charged phones and a little more setup time

contentBlocks.content: If one phone can keep the entire small-sided pitch clear and visible, start there. If players become too small in the frame or the goal areas are difficult to see, move to the two-phone setup. Good coverage matters more than using the newest phone.
What Happens After the Match

Once the match ends, the recording is uploaded for analysis. This football video analysis is powered by a custom computer vision and machine learning model trained around real small-sided football footage, where crowded pitches, quick transitions and grassroots camera angles look very different from professional broadcasts.

During the private beta, uploading and processing can currently take up to 45 minutes. This is an honest current limitation, not a promise of instant results. The upload flow is expected to improve as Pitchside develops, but connection speed, video length and footage quality can still affect the experience.
What helps Pitchside read the footage

items: A stable recording with minimal shaking
A clear, unobstructed view of the pitch
Enough height to separate players visually
Consistent lighting across the playing area
The full match recorded without missing sections

contentBlocks.content: Turn Your Recording Into Stats and Highlights

The value of recording a football match is not only being able to watch it again. Pitchside is being built to find the moments players care about and connect those moments to useful football statistics. The AI football highlights experience is designed to reduce the time spent searching through an entire match video.

headers: What Pitchside is being built to provide

cells: Highlights
Key moments from the match without manually searching through the full recording
Goals and assists
Events assigned to teams and individual players where the footage allows
Saves
Goalkeeper moments and saves identified from the recording
Passes and tackles
Core on-ball and defensive actions for teams and players
Leaderboards
Player comparisons across the statistics collected from matches

contentBlocks.content: Pitchside is still learning. Event detection and player assignment are improving during beta and will not be perfect in every match. Camera height, angle, lighting, obstructions and the distance between the phone and the action can all influence the result. Teams can use the free 5-a-side football stats tracker when they want to record supported match events manually.
Football Formats Supported
Pitchside is focused on small-sided football first. Its model has been developed around the speed, tighter spaces and repeated player actions found in amateur 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side matches.

cells: 5-a-side
Core training and development format
A single elevated phone may cover a compact pitch; two phones can improve goal-area detail
6-a-side
Supported small-sided format
Choose one or two phones according to the pitch width and available camera height
7-a-side
Supported small-sided format
Two phones may provide stronger coverage on larger pitches

contentBlocks.content: Full-size 11-a-side football is not the main focus of the current private beta. Pitchside is deliberately starting with the amateur small-sided formats its model has been trained to understand.
How to Set Up Your Phones

A careful setup gives you better footage and gives the Pitchside model a clearer view of the game. For exact camera positions, one-phone and two-phone diagrams, recommended heights and a match-day checklist, follow the football recording setup guide.

items: Charge every phone before leaving for the match.
Free enough storage for one uninterrupted full-match recording.
Clean the camera lens and switch the phone to landscape orientation.
Place the phone near the halfway line and above head height.
Use a stable tripod or mount and make sure it cannot fall into the playing area.
Frame both touchlines and the relevant goal before kick-off.
Record a short test clip and check that players remain visible across the pitch.
Start early, confirm the timer is running and leave the phone undisturbed.

contentBlocks.content: You do not need to choose an expensive mount to use Pitchside. Stability, safe positioning and enough height are the priorities. Detailed mount comparisons and buying recommendations belong in separate equipment guides rather than on this product page.
